targetAudience.primary: Architects and governance leaders designing self-improving agent systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands evaluation splits, versioned state, deployment, and rollback.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A model-generated procedure improvement can silently become future execution authority before independent evidence establishes that it should.

whyNow: Procedural Graphs provides a concrete primary-study mechanism that freezes active procedure state, mutates candidates offline, and admits changes only through structural checks plus disjoint held-out evidence.

externalHook.description: A self-improving worker writes a promising procedural change directly into the state that controls its next task.

coreProposition: Self-evolving procedures must remain candidate control state until an explicit adoption gate evaluates evidence not used to generate the proposal; the active procedure keeps a separate stable identity until that gate passes.

originalValue.description: Treats procedure mutation as controlled policy deployment with stable candidate identity, disjoint evidence, explicit adoption, durable rejection, freshness, and rollback.

readerTakeaway: Give models broad proposal freedom but narrow activation authority: preserve candidate/active separation and require acceptance evidence tied to exact identities and current risk.

supported: The study freezes the retained graph during inference and mutates candidates between batches.
Candidates face structural checks and disjoint validation before replacement.
Reported search history includes no-op rounds, structural rejection, and behavioral rejection.
Proposal, guidance, and solving can share one underlying model family.
unsupported: A claim that non-decreasing mean validation is sufficient for production safety
A claim of organizationally independent adjudication
A proof of crash-safe exactly-once activation
uncertain: Which safety dimensions belong in high-impact gates
How to make rejected candidates non-restorable

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument derives from public primary research and is independent of first-party projects.

decisionReason: The study gives a concrete candidate/adoption mechanism and explicit limitations suitable for a bounded governance analysis.
